claims.claim: In a phase 2 trial, retatrutide was compared against dulaglutide in participants with obesity and type 2 diabetes.
claims.quote: T2D trial: retatrutide (0.5, 4, 8, 12 mg) or placebo or dulaglutide (1.5 mg).

claims.claim: Retatrutide treatment was associated with improvements in metabolic health-related lipid and metabolite clusters in phase 2 trials.
claims.quote: Retatrutide was associated with changes in two metabolic clusters related to fatty acid oxidation and insulin resistance in a direction associated with improved metabolic health and reduced cardiovascular risk.

claims.claim: Retatrutide is a triple hormone receptor agonist targeting glucagon, GLP-1, and GIP receptors.
claims.quote: Retatrutide, a hormone receptor agonist targeting glucagon, glucagon-like peptide 1, and glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide, is being developed to treat obesity.

claims.claim: Phase II trials of retatrutide in obesity have shown up to 24% body weight reduction.
claims.quote: Phase I proof-of-concept studies led to phase II trials showing up to 24% body weight reduction and nearly 20 cm waist circumference reduction.

claims.claim: Gastrointestinal adverse effects are the most common adverse effects associated with retatrutide.
claims.quote: The most common adverse effects were gastrointestinal.

claims.claim: In pre-clinical cancer models, retatrutide reduced pancreatic cancer engraftment and tumor volume.
claims.quote: In pre-clinical models with significant retatrutide (RETA, LY3437943)-induced weight loss, pancreatic cancer engraftment was reduced, tumor onset was delayed, and progression was attenuated resulting in a 14-fold reduction in tumor volume compared to only 4-fold reduction in single agonist semaglutide-treated mice.

claims.claim: Retatrutide treatment in pre-clinical lung cancer models reduced tumor engraftment and volume.
claims.quote: RETA-induced protection extends to a lung cancer model with 50% reduced tumor engraftment, significantly delayed tumor onset, and mitigated tumor progression, with a 17-fold reduction in tumor volume compared to controls.

claims.claim: In murine models, retatrutide inhibited PI3K-AKT and NF-κB pathways in non-diabetic renal fibrosis.
claims.quote: In the UUO model, semaglutide effects were associated with PI3K-AKT inhibition, tirzepatide effects with PI3K-AKT inhibition and PPAR pathway activation, and retatrutide effects with concurrent inhibition of both PI3K-AKT and NF-κB pathways.

claims.claim: Retatrutide increased force of contraction in isolated human atrial preparations in a concentration-dependent manner.
claims.quote: We noted that cumulatively applied retatrutide starting at 10 nM (up to 100 nM the highest concentration tested) elevated FOC in HAP in a concentration- and time-dependent manner.

claims.claim: The TRANSCEND-CKD study evaluates the efficacy of retatrutide on glomerular filtration rate in adults with overweight/obesity and chronic kidney disease.
claims.quote: TRANSCEND-CKD is a double-blind, placebo-controlled, Phase 2b mechanistic study evaluating the efficacy of retatrutide in adults with overweight/obesity and CKD [estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) 25-75 mL/min/1.73 m2], with and without T2D.

claims.claim: Retatrutide is a novel triple receptor agonist targeting GLP-1, GIP, and glucagon receptors for the treatment of obesity and type 2 diabetes.
claims.quote: Retatrutide, a novel triple receptor agonist targeting glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1), Glucose-Dependent Insulinotropic Polypeptide (GIP), and glucagon receptors, represents a groundbreaking advancement in obesity and T2DM pharmacotherapy.

claims.claim: Retatrutide demonstrates dose-dependent weight loss and improvements in glycemic control in Phase 1 and 2 clinical trials.
claims.quote: Phase I and II clinical trials corroborate these findings, showing dose-dependent weight loss, reductions in Glycated Hemoglobin (HbA1c) levels, and improvements in liver steatosis and diabetic kidney disease.

claims.claim: Retatrutide has a mean half-life of approximately 6 days, supporting once-weekly dosing.
claims.quote: The pharmacokinetics of retatrutide were dose proportional and its mean half-life of approximately 6 days supported a once-weekly dosing.

claims.claim: Clinical trials for retatrutide have shown that gastrointestinal disorders are the most common adverse effects.
claims.quote: The safety profile was similar to GLP-1R agonists and glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide receptor/GLP-1R co-agonists, with gastrointestinal disorders being the most common adverse effects reported.

claims.claim: Retatrutide displays a robust intrinsic receptor activity hierarchy of GIPR > GLP-1R > GCGR.
claims.quote: Retatrutide showed a highly robust intrinsic GIPR>GLP-1R>GCGR hierarchy, while its quantitative human activation vector remained underidentified.

claims.claim: Early clinical data for retatrutide indicate potential hepatoprotective effects in patients with MASLD.
claims.quote: Emerging agents like cotadutide (a GLP-1/glucagon receptor agonist) and retatrutide (a GLP-1/GIP/glucagon triagonist) represent a novel therapeutic frontier, with early clinical data indicating potent hepatoprotective effects and favorable metabolic remodeling.

claims.claim: In US adults, overall obesity prevalence increased from 46.7% to 61.7% between 1999 and 2018.
claims.quote: Overall obesity prevalence rose from 46.7% to 61.7%

claims.claim: Clinical obesity in US adults was associated with a 1.46 hazard ratio for all-cause mortality compared to preclinical obesity.
claims.quote: Clinical obesity was associated with significantly higher risks of all-cause (HR 1.46, 95% CI 1.29–1.66) and cardiovascular (HR 1.65, 95% CI 1.29–2.10) mortality versus preclinical obesity.

claims.claim: Combined overweight and obesity prevalence among US midlife women aged 40-64 years increased from 49.2% in 1990 to 74.2% in 2021.
claims.quote: Combined overweight/obesity prevalence increased from 49.2% (95% uncertainty interval (UI) 45.8-52.2; 17.7 million (95% UI 16.5-18.8 million)) in 1990 to 74.2% (95% UI 68.8-79.1; 33.4 million (95% UI 31.0-35.6 million)) in 2021

claims.claim: Among US antiobesity medication users, 38.1% were classified as having pre-clinical obesity.
claims.quote: Of AOM users, 38.1% (n = 53,633) had pre-clinical obesity.

claims.claim: Clinical obesity in patients receiving bariatric surgery or antiobesity medications was associated with higher odds of post-treatment complications compared to pre-clinical obesity.
claims.quote: Clinical obesity was associated with higher odds of post-treatment complications (AOM: aOR 1.10, BS: aOR 1.39, both p < 0.001).

claims.claim: The age-standardized prevalence of clinical obesity in US adults nearly doubled from 14.3% in 1999-2000 to 26.6% in 2021-2023.
claims.quote: age-standardized prevalence of clinical obesity nearly doubled (14.3% to 26.6%; p < 0.001)

claims.claim: In the United States, the prevalence of adult obesity was 40.3% in 2021-2023.
claims.quote: prevalence falling to 40.3% in 2021-2023

claims.claim: In 2021, the prevalence of overweight and obesity in the United States ranged from 55.4% to 73.6% across jurisdictions.
claims.quote: mean O/OV prevalence was 67.72%, ranging from 55.4% in DC to 73.6% in WV

claims.claim: In a cross-sectional analysis of US adults from 2003-2004 and 2011-2014, higher serum DHA levels were associated with lower odds of central obesity.
claims.quote: DHA was significantly associated with lower odds of central obesity (OR: 0·83, 95 % CI: 0·73-0·95)

claims.claim: Network pharmacology analysis suggests DHA may act through TNF and IL-17 signaling pathways in the context of obesity-associated comorbidities.
claims.quote: Mechanistic exploration implicated DHA in TNF and IL-17 signalling pathways

claims.claim: In 2021, high BMI globally contributed to 5255 thyroid cancer-related deaths.
claims.quote: In 2021, high BMI contributed to 5255 thyroid cancer-related deaths (age-standardised mortality rate: 0.06 per 100 000) and 144 955 DALYs (age-standardised rate: 1.68 per 100 000)

claims.claim: The overall prevalence of clinical obesity among US adults from 2017 to 2020 was 9.7%.
claims.quote: Among 8037 participants, the overall prevalence of clinical obesity was 9.7% (95% CI, 8.9%-10.5%), with comparable prevalence in males (9.8%) and in females (9.6%).

claims.claim: No drug label records for retatrutide were found in the openFDA database.
claims.quote: No drug label records matching 'retatrutide' were found in the openFDA drug label database (search by generic name, brand name and substance name).

claims.claim: The FDA label for Orforglipron mentions the term obesity or weight management, but this does not confirm it is indicated for obesity.
